title: Outage: three new nodes join the cluster and never become usable

lines.text: 09:10 scanners: 50 of 90 replicas Pending; loading peak at 10:00

objective: Configure IP address management (IPAM) with Cilium: cluster-scope and Kubernetes host-scope modes, pod CIDRs per node, and cloud-native IPAM (ENI, Azure, GKE)
secondaryObjectives: Cilium component roles: what the agent, operator and proxy each own, and how they interact with the Kubernetes API

sources.cite: Isovalent, Cilium Certified Associate (CCA) exam page: Architecture 20%, Network Policy 18%, Service Mesh 16%, Network Observability 10%, Installation and Configuration 10%, Cluster Mesh 10%, eBPF 10%, BGP and External Networking 6%
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17 (a third-party page from the project's main contributor, not the CNCF curriculum; to verify against cncf/curriculum). The objective wording is the course seed's.

sources.cite: Cilium documentation, IP Address Management: Cluster Scope (Default)
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Relevant text: the Cilium operator, not Kubernetes, manages per-node PodCIDRs through the v2.CiliumNode resource, and the agent waits at start-up until spec.ipam.podCIDRs is populated; clusterPoolIPv4MaskSize cannot be changed; 'Don't change any existing elements of the clusterPoolIPv4PodCIDRList list'; 'If the pool is exhausted, add a new element to the list instead'; check the Error field under status.ipam.operator-status on each CiliumNode. The operator's error text, the agent-not-ready taint and the cilium-dbg output in the scenario are authored in Cilium's style (to verify).

brief.situation: You run the Kubernetes platform for Kestrel Logistics, a fictional freight company, on self-managed nodes with Cilium in cluster-pool IPAM mode. For the 10:00 loading peak, three nodes were added at 09:00 and the warehouse scanners' Deployment scaled from 40 to 90 replicas. The new nodes show as Ready to the cloud provider, but nothing is scheduled on them and 50 Pods are Pending.
handover: The cluster was installed with the Helm chart's IPAM settings copied from a lab: one /22 pool, /24 per node.
There were four nodes until this morning.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the operator's pool, the CiliumNode resources and the nodes.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

source.note: The loading peak starts at 10:00, 50 minutes after the report.

effects.finding: The new nodes carry Cilium's agent-not-ready taint: their agents never finished starting.

effects.finding: A /22 split into /24s is four node CIDRs; the mask size cannot be changed, so the pool needs another element.

plan.label: Check the address plan for a free range (nodes, Services, peers)
plan.why: Wait for the running command to finish.

effects.output:
ops@k8s-admin:~$ cat netplan/kestrel-ipam.md | grep -E 'nodes|services|vpn|free'
nodes:     172.20.0.0/24
services:  10.96.0.0/12
vpn peers: 10.0.4.0/22, 192.168.0.0/16

effects.finding: 10.0.8.0/21 is free and reserved for pods; 10.0.4.0/22 next door belongs to the VPN peers.

append.label: helm upgrade cilium --reuse-values --set ipam.operator.clusterPoolIPv4PodCIDRList=... (add 10.0.8.0/21)
append.available: not busy and (isNull(appendAt) and not changed)

effects.output:
ops@k8s-admin:~$ helm upgrade cilium cilium/cilium -n kube-system --reuse-values --set ipam.operator.clusterPoolIPv4PodCIDRList='{{10.0.0.0/22,10.0.8.0/21}}' && kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deploy/cilium-operator
Release "cilium" has been upgraded.
deployment.apps/cilium-operator restarted

effects.log: The existing element stays as it is; the new /21 gives the operator eight more /24s.

effects.output:
ops@k8s-admin:~$ helm upgrade cilium cilium/cilium -n kube-system --reuse-values --set ipam.operator.clusterPoolIPv4PodCIDRList='{{10.0.0.0/16}}' && kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deploy/cilium-operator ds/cilium
Release "cilium" has been upgraded.

effects.log: Changing an existing element of the pool leaves the nodes' allocations inconsistent with it, and the /16 now overlaps the VPN peers' 10.0.4.0/22: traffic to running Pods and to the peers breaks.

mask.label: Set clusterPoolIPv4MaskSize to 26 so the /22 holds more nodes

effects.output:
ops@k8s-admin:~$ helm upgrade cilium cilium/cilium -n kube-system --reuse-values --set ipam.operator.clusterPoolIPv4MaskSize=26
Release "cilium" has been upgraded.
(the operator keeps the existing /24 allocations; w5 to w7 still have no pod CIDR)

effects.log: The mask size cannot be changed on a running pool: nothing moves.

effects.output:
ops@k8s-admin:~$ kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart ds/cilium
daemonset.apps/cilium restarted

effects.log: The agents restart one by one, briefly disturbing the healthy nodes; the new ones still wait for a CIDR the pool does not have.

writeup.question: For the record: why the new nodes never became usable, what you changed in the pool, and what you left alone.

parts.label: Why
parts.criteria: Traces the taint to the agent waiting on the operator's exhausted pool.
parts.modelAnswer: The new nodes kept the agent-not-ready taint because their agents waited for a pod CIDR; their CiliumNodes showed the operator's pool exhausted. A /22 at /24 per node is four node CIDRs, and four nodes already had them.

parts.label: Change
parts.criteria: Adds a free range as a new element, checked against the plan.
parts.modelAnswer: Added 10.0.8.0/21, free and reserved for pods in the address plan, as a second element of clusterPoolIPv4PodCIDRList, and restarted the operator; the new nodes got /24s from it.

parts.label: Left alone
parts.criteria: Explains why the existing element and the mask stay.
parts.modelAnswer: The existing element and the mask size cannot be changed safely; replacing the pool with a /16 would have broken running Pods' routes and overlapped the VPN peers' range.

source.cite: Infrastructure outcome profile (docs/sims.md 9.2, 22.10), tightened to 50 minutes for this case
source.note: The loading peak starts at 10:00; the scenario's own timing.
No second fault: a pool changed in place, or agents restarted for nothing.

expertPath.text: Pending: agent-not-ready taint on w5-w7; the agent waits for a pod CIDR; CiliumNodes: pool exhausted; config: one /22 at /24 per node; the plan: 10.0.8.0/21 free.
Add 10.0.8.0/21 as a second element and restart the operator.

brokeExisting.headline: A bigger pool, a broken one
brokeExisting.body: Existing elements of the cluster pool must not change. Add a new, free range as another element instead.

peakMissed.headline: Three idle nodes at the peak
peakMissed.body: Restarting agents and changing the mask do not create CIDRs. The CiliumNode error and the pool's size showed the pool had none left.

fixed.headline: Good: extend, don't edit
fixed.body: You followed the chain from Pending Pods to the operator's pool, checked the address plan for a free range, added it without touching the existing element or the mask, and confirmed all 90 replicas ran.

gaps.headline: Extended, with gaps
gaps.body: The criteria show what was left: reading the CiliumNodes and the config, checking the plan, verifying, or a needless restart.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: No record was written before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: The new nodes carry Cilium's agent-not-ready taint because their agents wait for the operator to put a pod CIDR on their CiliumNode, and the CiliumNodes show the operator's pool exhausted: a /22 split into /24s is four node CIDRs, all used. The mask size cannot be changed and existing elements of the pool must not be edited, so add a new element from free address space, checked against the plan so it does not overlap nodes, Services or the VPN peers, and restart the operator. Restarting the agents changes nothing and disturbs healthy nodes. Confirm the new nodes get CIDRs and the replicas run before 10:00.
